questions.question: In Roald Dahl's The BFG, what does the giant catch in his net and blow into children's bedrooms?
questions.explanation: The BFG keeps the dreams he catches in jars, and blows the good ones in through children's windows with a long trumpet.

questions.question: Who owns the chocolate factory in Charlie and the Chocolate Factory?
questions.explanation: Wonka hid just five Golden Tickets in his chocolate bars, and Charlie found the very last one.

questions.question: In The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, which sweet does the White Witch tempt Edmund with?
questions.explanation: It was enchanted Turkish Delight, so the more Edmund ate, the more he wanted.

questions.question: In Matilda, what is the name of the fearsome head teacher?
questions.explanation: Roald Dahl tells us Miss Trunchbull once threw the hammer for Britain at the Olympics.

questions.question: Which book do these emoji describe?
questions.explanation: James travels across the ocean in a giant peach with a centipede, an earthworm, a spider and other huge minibeasts.

questions.question: Which book do these emoji describe?
options: We're Going on a Bear Hunt
questions.explanation: In the very first story Pooh floats up to a bees' nest on a balloon, pretending to be a little black rain cloud.

questions.question: Which book do these emoji describe?
questions.explanation: The clever mouse tricks a fox, an owl and a snake, and then the Gruffalo himself.

questions.question: Which book do these emoji describe?
questions.explanation: The crocodile swallowed a clock, so Captain Hook can hear it ticking as it comes after him.

questions.question: In David Walliams' Gangsta Granny, what does Ben's granny tell him she secretly used to be?
questions.explanation: Granny says she was the international jewel thief known as the Black Cat, and the pair plan to steal the Crown Jewels.

questions.question: Which Jacqueline Wilson character lives in a children's home she calls the Dumping Ground?
questions.explanation: Tracy first appeared in The Story of Tracy Beaker in 1991.

questions.question: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, who holds a never-ending tea party with the March Hare and the Dormouse?
questions.explanation: In the book the Hatter has quarrelled with Time, so it is always six o'clock and always teatime.

questions.question: Which fairy-tale character leaves a trail of breadcrumbs in the forest, only for the birds to eat them?
questions.explanation: The first time, Hansel dropped shiny white pebbles instead, which worked much better.

questions.question: In Roald Dahl's The Twits, what does Mr Twit smear on the branches of the Big Dead Tree to catch birds?
questions.explanation: The glue was so sticky that any bird landing on the tree could not fly away, ready for the Twits' Bird Pie.

questions.question: In Michael Morpurgo's War Horse, what is the name of the horse?
questions.explanation: The whole story is told by Joey himself, who is sent to France in the First World War.

questions.question: In Treasure Island, what is the name of Long John Silver's parrot?
questions.explanation: The parrot is named after the pirate whose treasure everyone is hunting, and squawks 'Pieces of eight!'

questions.question: Which novel begins 'It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife'?
questions.explanation: Jane Austen published it in 1813, having first called it First Impressions.

questions.question: Which Charles Dickens character says, 'Please, sir, I want some more'?
questions.explanation: Oliver asks for a second bowl of gruel in the workhouse, and is punished for it.

questions.question: In which Italian city is Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet set?
questions.explanation: Shakespeare liked Verona enough to open The Two Gentlemen of Verona there too.

questions.question: Which novel gave the world the phrases 'Big Brother' and 'Room 101'?
questions.explanation: George Orwell published it in 1949.

questions.question: Which book do these emoji describe?
options: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
questions.explanation: In L. Frank Baum's book Dorothy's magic shoes are silver; the 1939 film made them ruby.

questions.question: In Moby-Dick, what is the name of the captain obsessed with hunting the white whale?
questions.explanation: The novel opens with one of the most famous lines in literature: 'Call me Ishmael.'

questions.question: Which book do these emoji describe?
options: Around the World in Eighty Days
questions.explanation: In Daniel Defoe's 1719 novel the shipwrecked Crusoe is stunned to find a single human footprint in the sand.

questions.question: Which book do these emoji describe?
questions.explanation: Mary Shelley began writing it aged just 18, during a stormy summer by Lake Geneva in 1816.

questions.question: Which of the Brontë siblings wrote Wuthering Heights?
questions.explanation: It was Emily Brontë's only novel, published in 1847 under the name Ellis Bell.

questions.question: In Tolkien's The Hobbit, what is the name of the dragon?
questions.explanation: Smaug sleeps on a vast hoard of treasure under the Lonely Mountain.

questions.question: In which Shakespeare play does a character cry 'Out, damned spot!'?
questions.explanation: Lady Macbeth says it while sleepwalking, trying to scrub her guilt from her hands.

questions.question: Which novel is narrated by Nick Carraway?
questions.explanation: F. Scott Fitzgerald published it in 1925; Nick is Gatsby's neighbour on Long Island.

questions.question: George Eliot was the pen name of which writer?
questions.explanation: Mary Ann Evans wrote Middlemarch and Silas Marner under her male pen name.

questions.question: In Bram Stoker's Dracula, at which English seaside town does the Count come ashore?
questions.explanation: He leaps from a wrecked ship in the shape of a large dog; Stoker had holidayed in Whitby in 1890.

questions.question: Who wrote the nonsense poem The Owl and the Pussy-cat?
questions.explanation: The pair go to sea in a beautiful pea-green boat and dine on mince and slices of quince.
